hero.caption: View across a portion of Lake Springfield, looking south from Marine Point toward the railroad tracks (formerly Illinois Central, now Canadian National). The town known as Crow's Mill or Cotton Hill was formerly located beneath the water.

images.caption: The Crow's Mill Pub in the Toronto neighborhood of Springfield, Illinois, which occupies the relocated North Crow's Mill schoolhouse built in the early 20th century. The original location of the schoolhouse is now under Lake Springfield.

images.caption: Railroad bridge across the former Sugar Creek channel in Lake Springfield (Illinois). Owned and operated by the Canadian National Railroad, originally built by the St. Louis and Chicago Railway, and beginning in 1900 owned and operated by the Illinois Central Railroad. View is from the west (upstream) side. Red and green lights and arrows tell boaters to bear to the right going through the bridge; a buoy in front of the bridge warns boaters to reduce speed.
